name: Question 8
problem:
A body of mass $50\,\text{kg}$ is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the body's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the body is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=4.9\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find the equation for the velocity $v(t).$ Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the body are the weight due to gravity and drag.

Question 8
?

A body of mass 50kg is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let v(t) be the body's velocity, in meters per second, t≥0 seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction. The air resistance on the body is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality k=4.9kg/m and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find the equation for the velocity v(t). Assume the acceleration due to gravity is g=9.8m/s2, and the only forces acting on the body are the weight due to gravity and drag.

a
v(t)=10tanh⁡(110gt)
b
 v(t)=110tanh⁡(110gt)
c
 v(t)=tanh⁡(110gt)
d
 v(t)=tanh⁡(10gt)
e
 v(t)=10tanh⁡(gt)
